body:
### Problem

Registering custom EditorConfig properties is public API (`:help
editorconfig-properties`), but once the total passes 18, opening any
`.editorconfig` file errors and property names lose their highlighting:

```
Error in Syntax Autocommands for "*"..function <SNR>51_SynSet[26]..script
/usr/share/nvim/runtime/syntax/editorconfig.vim, line 16:
E5108: Lua: [string ":lua"]:2: invalid key: 21
stack traceback:
    [C]: in function 'syntax'
    [string ":lua"]:2: in main chunk
```

`runtime/syntax/editorconfig.vim:14-15` highlights the property names with:

```lua
local props = vim.tbl_keys(require('editorconfig').properties)
vim.cmd.syntax { 'keyword', 'editorconfigProperty', unpack(props) }
```

`vim.cmd.<name>{...}` moves only the first `VIM_CMD_ARG_MAX` positional
arguments into `args` (`runtime/lua/vim/_core/editor.lua`, currently 20). The
rest stay on the table as integer keys and `nvim_cmd` rejects them as unknown
fields, hence `invalid key: 21`. Two of the twenty are `keyword` and the group
name, so the syntax file breaks as soon as more than 18 properties exist.

Nvim registers 10 properties itself, so a plugin may add at most 8 before
breaking the syntax file for every `.editorconfig` its users open. The error
names only Nvim's runtime, giving no hint which plugin caused it. Found from a
plugin registering 13 custom properties.

This is not a regression: `VIM_CMD_ARG_MAX` has been there since `vim.cmd`
became indexable (#19238), predating the syntax file (added 2023-07-20).

### Steps to reproduce

[minimal.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31083284/minimal.zip)

`minimal.lua` (based on `contrib/minimal.lua`; no plugins required):

```lua
local N = tonumber(vim.env.EC_REPRO_N) or 9
for i = 1, N do
    require("editorconfig").properties["custom_property_" .. i] = function() end
end
```

Any `.editorconfig` file, e.g.:

```ini
root = true

[*]
indent_style = space
```

Then:

```
nvim --clean -u minimal.lua .editorconfig
```

The attached `run.sh` walks the boundary. Identical on release and nightly:

```
NVIM v0.12.2
 7 custom + 10 builtin = 17 properties: ok
 8 custom + 10 builtin = 18 properties: ok
 9 custom + 10 builtin = 19 properties: FAIL  E5108: Lua: [string ":lua"]:2: invalid key: 21
10 custom + 10 builtin = 20 properties: FAIL  E5108: Lua: [string ":lua"]:2: invalid key: 21

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1317+g64a301184e
 7 custom + 10 builtin = 17 properties: ok
 8 custom + 10 builtin = 18 properties: ok
 9 custom + 10 builtin = 19 properties: FAIL  E5108: Lua: [string ":lua"]:2: invalid key: 21
10 custom + 10 builtin = 20 properties: FAIL  E5108: Lua: [string ":lua"]:2: invalid key: 21
```

### Expected behavior

`.editorconfig` opens without error and its property names are highlighted,
however many properties are registered.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1317+g64a301184e (nightly, also reproduced on v0.12.2)

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

Not applicable: Vim has neither built-in EditorConfig support nor `vim.cmd`.

### Operating system/version

Fedora 43, Linux 7.0.14-101.fc43.x86_64

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.47.4 (reproduces headless; the terminal is not material)

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-kitty

### Installation

Nightly tarball from GitHub releases; also reproduced with a release build installed via bob.

comment_data.body:
This seems to fix the problem:
```diff
diff --git a/runtime/lua/vim/_core/editor.lua b/runtime/lua/vim/_core/editor.lua
index 3d876d2187..348679b794 100644
--- a/runtime/lua/vim/_core/editor.lua
+++ b/runtime/lua/vim/_core/editor.lua
@@ -437,8 +437,6 @@ vim.funcref = function(viml_func_name)
   return vim.fn[viml_func_name]
 end
 
-local VIM_CMD_ARG_MAX = 20
-
 --- Executes Vimscript (|Ex-command|s).
 ---
 --- Can be indexed with a command name to get a function, thus you can write `vim.cmd.echo(…)`
@@ -502,7 +500,7 @@ vim.cmd = setmetatable({}, {
         -- Move indexed positions in opts to opt.args
         if opts[1] and not opts.args then
           opts.args = {}
-          for i = 1, VIM_CMD_ARG_MAX do
+          for i = 1, #opts do
             if not opts[i] then
               break
             end
```

title: syntax/editorconfig.vim breaks when more than 18 EditorConfig properties are registered
